title: Extraction of Microremains from Archaeological Human Dental Calculus
author: Elena Fiorin
materials: Write the weight on the plastic tube.

steps.title: Select and document DC sample
steps.instruction: Choose a dental calculus (DC) piece that is not powdered; record its size, texture, colour, quantity, and any dental pathologies with a photograph and written description; avoid teeth with restorations; label the tooth according to the archaeological report and note the sampling strategy for downstream analyses (PLM, aDNA, proteomics, etc.).

steps.title: Remove DC from tooth
steps.instruction: Wear gloves, prepare a clean work surface (aluminium foil or plexiglass board) and optionally collect surrounding soil for contamination controls; place the tooth or mandible/maxilla on the surface; use a dental scaler (metal or plastic) to detach the calculus without scratching enamel; immediately transfer the calculus into a labelled plastic tube using tweezers; place the tube in a labelled plastic bag; decontaminate the work area and all instruments after each sampling with bleach, alcohol, or boiling water.

substeps.instruction: 2.1 Wear gloves and set up a clean work area using aluminium foil or a plexiglass board; optionally collect soil from the burial context for later contaminant assessment.
2.2 Position the tooth/bone and use a dental scaler (or plastic instrument) to remove the DC, taking care not to damage enamel.
2.3 Transfer the DC directly into a plastic tube with tweezers; label the tube with site, tooth, and DC position; store the tube in a labelled plastic bag.
2.4 Clean the work area and all tools after sampling with bleach, alcohol, or boiling water.

steps.title: Store DC sample
steps.instruction: Keep the DC in its labelled plastic tube; ensure the calculus is completely dry before transport to the laboratory; if the sample is wet at excavation, dry or decontaminate it as soon as possible.

steps.title: Weight DC sample
steps.instruction: Using a precision balance, weigh the calculus before any decontamination (and optionally after) and record the weight on the tube label.

substeps.instruction: Place a piece of aluminium foil (or filtered paper) on the balance pan, close the glass doors and tare.
Open the doors, place the DC on the foil with tweezers, close the doors and read the weight.
Write the measured weight on the plastic tube (repeat after decontamination if desired).

steps.title: Decontaminate DC sample
steps.instruction: Remove loosely attached soil and the mineralised surface layer, then wash and dry the calculus before extraction.

substeps.instruction: 5.1 Add drops of ultrapure water to each tube; optionally place tubes on a digital orbital shaker at 170 RPM for 3–24 h to accelerate soil release.

5.2 Under a stereomicroscope, hold the DC with tweezers and use an acupuncture needle (or regular needle) soaked in 0.5 M or 1.5 M HCl to scrape off the external mineralised layer; for very small samples, use a nylon‑bristle paintbrush instead of the needle; rinse with ultrapure water as needed.
5.3 Wash the cleaned DC in a minicentrifuge with ultrapure water up to three times, discarding the supernatant after each spin.
5.4 Dry the DC and store it in a new labelled plastic tube, or proceed directly to the dissolution step.
5.5 Collect the removed ‘dirty’ waste for later contamination checks.

steps.title: Dissolve DC and prepare slides
steps.instruction: Dissolve the cleaned calculus in HCl, mount the solution on slides with glycerol‑water, and observe by PLM while maintaining contamination controls.

substeps.instruction: 6.1 Add a few drops of 0.5–1.5 M HCl to the tube containing the DC and let it dissolve completely.
6.2 Once dissolved, mount the solution on microscope slides using a 50:50 (v/v) mixture of glycerol and ultrapure water; perform this step under a fume hood to avoid contamination.

6.3 Observe the prepared slides by polarized light microscopy (PLM); ensure all instruments and work surfaces have been cleaned with bleach, alcohol, or boiling water and check slides for any residual contaminants.
